title: Mini trial slate — latency & cost quicksheet
summary: Compact single-page tracker for a focused latency vs cost sweep across small model variants and batching/kv-cache toggles.
content:
Mini trial slate (keepsake):

Goal: quick, re-runnable capture of latency vs cost tradeoffs when toggling KV cache and small batching for 7B-class models. Not an exhaustive benchmark — targeted, iterative notes for prioritizing follow-ups.

Context: running on local dev dedicated pool (p4d-ish sim). Sequence length kept at 512 for consistency. Token accounting: prompt+gen. Cost is rough estimate based on instance cost + GPU seconds amortized per 1k tokens.

Quick table (raw runs):

RunID | Model          | Quant  | Batch | KVcache | Seq | toks/s | p50_ms | p95_ms | cost_per_1k | perf_score | notes
----- | ------------- | ------ | ----- | ------- | --- | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------------ | ---------- | -----
r001  | redwood-7b     | q4_0   | 1     | off     | 512 | 85     | 210    | 480    | $1.85        | 0.66       | baseline small batch=1
r002  | redwood-7b     | q4_0   | 4     | off     | 512 | 220    | 75     | 190    | $1.02        | 0.78       | batching helps, higher throughput
r003  | redwood-7b     | q4_0   | 4     | on      | 512 | 310    | 45     | 120    | $0.86        | 0.91       | KV cache big win for repeated prefixes
r004  | redwood-7b-lite| q4_0   | 4     | on      | 512 | 420    | 32     | 80     | $0.62        | 0.95       | lighter weights (pruned) -> good perf/cost
r005  | redwood-7b     | q3_8   | 8     | on      | 512 | 500    | 28     | 65     | $0.58        | 0.90       | more aggressive quant gives best cost but watch quality
r006  | redwood-3b     | q4_0   | 8     | on      | 512 | 760    | 18     | 40     | $0.36        | 0.70       | small model, much cheaper but eval quality lower

Notes / interpretation:
- KV cache: the largest single reduction in p50 and p95 for this workload (r002 -> r003). If application has stable prefixes, enable by default.
- Batching: improves tokens/sec strongly but watch p95 tail for small interactive SLOs. Batch=4 appears a good sweet spot for 7b.
- Quantization: q3_8 in r005 lowers cost the most but requires an eval pass for hallucination rate (schedule).
- redwood-7b-lite looks promising as a deploy variant for internal beta (r004) — need AB test on quality metrics.

Quick TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Run prompt-sensitivity sweep on r005 vs r003 for 200 eval prompts (metric: BLEU-like or QA exact-match). (Owner: Mira)
- [ ] Re-run r003 with seq=1024 to see memory knee and token/sec drop (Owner: me).
- [ ] Add a tiny synthetic tail-load test to capture p99 for batch=4 (JIRA: INF-219 task).

Commands to reproduce (local dev alias):
- bench_run --model redwood-7b --quant q4_0 --batch 4 --kv on --seq 512 --run-id r003 --out csv
- quick-compare --inputs evalset_200.json --a r003.csv --b r005.csv --metrics em,f1,latency

Open questions / scribbles:
- If most production requests have short prefix variability, maybe auto-kv eviction + predictive caching helps more than naive on/off. cost/benefit math next.
- How do these numbers shift on a slower network (adds 10–20ms)? Likely p50 shifts but tokens/sec remains same; need network-aware routing policy test.

Decision hints for next-stage:
- If quality of q3_8 == q4_0 on eval set (<=1% regression), prefer q3_8 for Dedicated low-tier to cut unit cost.
- For interactive UI (SLO p50 < 100ms), consider redwood-7b-lite or 3b with model-variant routing.

Misc scratch links:
- GH runtime PR: redwood-inference/runtime#432 (kernel fallback change)
- Short note in Confluence: latency-benchnotes (see section "mini-slate results")

End of mini slate. Keep this small and re-run when a new kernel lands or a different quant profile is added.

Handy abbreviations used: q4_0 = quant q4 with profile 0; q3_8 = q3 with 8-bit hybrid; KVcache = prefix KV caching; toks/s = tokens per second; p50/p95 in ms.
